one_month_reasoning: Correction from round 1: Q3 results are not on 2026-10-29. Materion has not announced a date. It has reported Q3 exactly 33 days after fiscal quarter end every year from 2022 to 2025, and Q3 2026 ends Oct 2, which points to Wednesday 2026-11-04 (MarketBeat also estimates Nov 4). The 1-month close is Friday 2026-10-30, since 2026-11-01 is a Sunday, so the print falls after the window. What does fall inside it are value-chain reads in my lane: late-October reports from WFE and semis-materials names (Lam, Entegris, MKS, Ultra Clean), connector demand (Amphenol), and the aerospace alloy peers (Carpenter, ATI, Howmet, Hexcel). The SEMI mid-year forecast (+21.8% WFE in 2027) makes positive semis read-across more likely than negative, but it is largely known. Against that, the +16% move on Oct 1-2 has no identified filing or news catalyst and could partly reverse. So I take a lognormal with a median of ~$309.5, a small give-back, and sigma 15.8% over ~20 trading days. That is about 56% annualized ex-earnings, a bit above the supervisor's 15.5% to allow for peer prints and theme flow. I removed the earnings-jump widening I used in round 1.

fair_value.method: Blend of 25x NTM P/E on 2028E EPS of $9.92 ($248, 60% weight) and 19x NTM EV/EBITDA on Oct-2027 NTM standardized EBITDA of ~$292M, less ~$0.36B net debt, over 21.1M diluted shares ($246, 40% weight). Both multiples now sit at or just above the 10-peer medians (24.3x fwd P/E, 18.8x fwd EV/EBITDA). The result is ~$247.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: FY2026 EPS $7.00 (guide midpoint) -> FY2027E $8.55 (+22%, ~1% above consensus $8.48) -> FY2028E $9.92 (+16%); 25x NTM P/E at Oct-2027 (peer median 24.3x)

inputs_detail.derivation: I start from MarketBeat consensus of $8.48 and add ~1% because value-chain demand is ahead of what sell-side models assume. SEMI's mid-year forecast lifted 2027 WFE growth from +7.3% (Dec-2025 forecast) to +21.8%, Amphenol IT datacom is +63% organic, and the FY27 request lifts missile procurement by 188%. This is labelled above consensus. I cut it from round 1's $8.60.

SEMI forecasts WFE +14.1% in 2028 (to ~$200B) and total equipment at a record $229B. Elmore beryllium capacity (customer-funded) adds volume. I fade growth slightly against JX's +60% target capacity adding competition in sputter targets.

The median forward P/E of the 10 comps listed in `comps` is 24.3x: aerospace alloys CRS 29.0, ATI 33.1, HWM 39.7, HXL 32.9, KALU 14.5; semis materials and supply chain ENTG 37.1, ESI 19.6, MKSI 17.8, UCTT 15.1, JX 19.0. A mix-weighted view (half the aero-alloy median of 32.9x, half the semis-materials median of 19.0x) gives ~26x. MTRN today trades at 39.4x. I cannot argue a persistent premium to the median (see comps_summary), so I use 25x, about 3% above the median and inside the 14.5-39.7x range.

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.inputs: TTM standardized EBITDA $205.45M grown ~15%/yr for ~2.5 years to Oct-2027 NTM (~FY2028) ~$292M x 19x = EV $5.54B; less net debt ~$0.36B = equity $5.18B / 21.1M = ~$246

inputs_detail.input: TTM EBITDA (S&P-standardized, same basis as peers)
inputs_detail.derivation: I use the same data vendor and basis as the peer multiples so the comparison is like-for-like. Round 1 used company-adjusted EBITDA, which is not comparable to peer figures.

TTM centre ~Jan-2026 to FY2028 centre ~Jul-2028 is ~2.5 years at ~15%/yr (x1.42). That is in line with StockAnalysis's 15.9% 3-yr revenue growth forecast for MTRN, Q2 value-added sales growth of ~15%, and SEMI WFE growth of +21.8%/+14.1%.
Company-defined net debt is $420.7M (10-Q). H1 FCF was $39M with Q2 alone $58.7M; I assume ~$60M of net paydown over 15 months after capex (~$100M) and the dividend.

The 10-peer median forward EV/EBITDA is 18.8x (range 7.6x-30.4x), derived as EV / (TTM EBITDA x (1 + next-FY consensus revenue growth)) for each peer. MTRN on the same basis is 29.4x today. I use the median, rounded to 19x.

bear.story: The AI/WFE cycle digests in 2027 (SEMI's +21.8% forecast gets cut), Electronic Materials margins fall back from 32% toward the mid-20s, JX's new target capacity pressures pricing, and missile-procurement reconciliation money slips. EPS stalls near $7.5-8 and the stock de-rates to the semis-materials peer cluster (~19-22x): ~$180.

base.story: Backlog converts and FY2027 EPS reaches ~$8.5, in line with or slightly above consensus. The market rolls forward to FY2028E of ~$9.9 but compresses the multiple from 39x toward the high-20s as growth normalises, between the 10-peer median (24x) and the aero-alloy cluster (33x). Momentum and the scarcity theme keep it above my $247 fundamental value: ~$275.

bull.story: WFE grows ~22% in 2027 and ~14% in 2028 as SEMI forecasts, AI datacom (Amphenol) keeps pulling Be-Cu and clad strip, missile funding is enacted at +188%, and Elmore sells out. EPS reaches $11+ for 2028E and the stock holds a ~38x aero-alloy-premium multiple (HWM/ENTG level): ~$420.

thesis_break_reason: A close below ~$188 means the stock has broken the 2026-07-29 closing low ($189.34), from just before the Q2 beat and raise, and trades at ~22x FY2027 consensus ($8.48), which is the semis-materials peer cluster with no premium left. With my fair value at ~$247, that is ~24% below fundamental value. It most likely reflects a fundamental break (backlog or guidance cut from a WFE/AI digestion, Electronic Materials margin reversal, or defense funding slippage) rather than ordinary ~55-60% volatility.

reasoning: Round 2 changes. (1) The supervisor's fact-check moved Q3 results to most likely 2026-11-04, outside the 1-month window, so I removed the earnings widening from ladder_1m. (2) I replaced the weak cryptobriefing '$209.5B 2027 WFE' figure with SEMI's own mid-year forecast: WFE $143.9B in 2026, +21.8% in 2027, +14.1% in 2028 toward ~$200B. That is still a strong upgrade from SEMI's Dec-2025 call of +7.3% for 2027, so the value-chain demand picture holds, but the level is lower than I used. (3) The biggest change is valuation. The supervisor asked whether Carpenter's 32x fits a business that is 54% semis pass-through by net sales with flat 2022-25 EPS, and the required 10-peer comps answer no. Forward P/E across five aero-alloy and five semis-materials peers has a median of 24.3x (aero cluster ~33x, semis-materials cluster ~19x), and forward EV/EBITDA has a median of 18.8x. MTRN's next-year EPS growth (+21% consensus) is below the peer median (+24.6%), its margins on net sales are lower, and its EPS history is more cyclical. I cannot argue a persistent premium, so both multiples move to about the median (25x P/E, 19x EV/EBITDA). With EPS slightly above consensus, fair value falls from $325 to ~$247. (4) For the 12-month distribution I do not set the median at fair value. Multiples converge slowly, momentum and the beryllium-scarcity theme are real, and the value chain is strengthening. So the median is ~$278, about midway between fair value and spot, with a lognormal sigma of ~0.45 and a 15% fat-tail component (sigma 0.75). That gives P(>= $312) ~40%, down from 51.5%. The scenario mean is ~$288. My view is now a little below the supervisor's ($280 FV, P(>=312) ~45%) because the peer set says the market pays less for this mix than the aero-alloy names alone suggest. Research this round: 3 searches and ~22 fetches, mostly peer statistics and forecast pages and SEMI coverage. The semi.org page returned 403, so the WFE figures come from search snippets of the SEMI release plus Circuits Assembly coverage. Twelve Data statistics are plan-restricted.

comps_summary.mtrn_multiples_in_fair_value: P/E 25x (+3% vs the 24.3x median; inside range). EV/EBITDA 19x (+1% vs the 18.8x median; inside range).
comps_summary.justification: The peer set splits into two clusters. Aerospace/defense alloy names (CRS, ATI, HWM, HXL) trade at 29-40x forward earnings, with KALU at 14.5x as a commodity-exposed outlier. Semis materials and supply-chain names (ENTG 37x aside: ESI, MKSI, UCTT and the direct sputter-target competitor JX Advanced Metals) trade at 15-20x. Materion straddles both. Semiconductor is ~54% of H1 2026 net sales (mostly pass-through metal in Electronic Materials), and A&D is ~20-24% of value-added sales. A blend of the two cluster medians gives ~26x, close to the overall 24.3x median. I tested each premium argument against evidence. Growth: MTRN's consensus next-year EPS growth (+21%) is below the peer median (+24.6%), so there is no growth premium. Margins and returns: Q2 2026 adjusted EBITDA was 23.3% of value-added sales but only ~12% of net sales, and standardized TTM EBITDA of $205M on $2.10B revenue (~10%) is below CRS (~26%), HWM (~31%) or ENTG; no premium. Cyclicality: adjusted EPS was roughly flat over 2022-2025 before the 2026 jump, and Electronic Materials margins swung from 23% to 32% in a year, so MTRN is at least as cyclical as the peers; if anything a discount. Balance sheet: net debt of $420.7M is ~2x TTM standardized EBITDA, average for the group; neutral. The one structural positive is beryllium. MTRN is the only integrated Western producer, a defense prime funded $65M of new capacity, and IBC exited cast Be-Al. But that business is a minority of earnings, and Ulba (Kazakhstan) plus JX's +60% target capacity show the moat is not total. Net, I cannot rigorously show a premium that persists through Oct-2027. So I moved both multiples to the peer median (25x and 19x, rounded) and recorded the change in `revisions`. Today's 39x is outside what the peers justify; I treat that gap as momentum and theme premium, which my distribution partly keeps (median $278) but my fair value does not.
